courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Medical Knowledge I
courses.description: Uses a clinically focused framework and real-world conditions to provide a clinically relevant integrated understanding of functional human gross anatomy, microscopic anatomy (histology), and general embryology. This foundational knowledge prepares students to understand the structural and cellular concepts essential for future clinical study in the biomedical sciences and health professions. Enrollment in Medical Knowledge I alongside other courses in the Medical Knowledge sequence is not recommended, as the course content is designed to be cumulative and sequential. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Medical Knowledge II
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive foundation for clinically relevant molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying human physiology. Using patient-centered, case-based learning, students examine how molecular processes maintain health and drive responses to physiological and environmental challenges. This course emphasizes applying biochemical principles to interpret clinical presentations, strengthening the connection between basic science and clinical practice while developing essential reasoning skills for future health professionals. Enrollment in Medical Knowledge II alongside other courses in the Medical Knowledge sequence is not recommended, as the course content is designed to be cumulative and sequential. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Medical Knowledge IV
courses.description: Provides an integrated examination of pharmacology and therapeutic interventions in human disease. Students explore how pharmaceuticals interact with biological systems to treat disease and improve patient outcomes, emphasizing mechanisms of action, drug-body interactions, and therapies for infectious diseases. Rather than memorizing individual medications, students will focus on the biological basis of therapeutic strategies and their clinical application. Through patient-centered, case-based learning, students will develop evidence-based clinical reasoning skills essential for future healthcare professionals. Enrollment in Medical Knowledge IV alongside other courses in the Medical Knowledge sequence is not recommended, as the course content is designed to be cumulative and sequential. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Health Innovation I
courses.description: Examines the foundational principles of healthcare and community innovation. Students will consider why innovation is necessary in modern health systems, including the distinctions among innovation, research, and quality improvement. The course emphasizes approaches that ensure innovation efforts are responsive to patient and community needs through empathy, qualitative methods, stakeholder engagement, and inclusive problem framing. Through systems thinking, social determinants of health, equity frameworks, and patient-centered design, students will develop the skills needed to identify meaningful healthcare challenges and opportunities for innovation.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Identify—Healthcare Ecosystem and Need Identification
courses.description: An overview of the healthcare ecosystem, the healthcare innovation process, and value creation. Emphasis is placed on key concepts and principles essential for efficiently designing and managing healthcare delivery systems. Focused on uncovering innovation opportunities through in-depth identification and analysis of unmet, underserved, and unarticulated stakeholder needs using qualitative, analytical, and design thinking methodologies. Emphasizes critical thinking and creativity and prepares students to recognize and select opportunities that can be developed into successful innovations. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Innovate—Healthcare Innovation Process
courses.description: Guides students through the healthcare innovation process, from ideation and concept generation to product and process design and development. Students will learn how to balance cost, quality, and usability in product development and how to integrate technology trends, user feedback, and various analyses for concept development and business case preparation. An in-depth exploration of principles and methodologies for rapid and efficient prototyping is included, as are the intricacies of process management and effective strategies for managing healthcare innovation. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit.

courses.subject: HBSE
courses.title: Implement—Healthcare Business Strategy and New Venture Implementation
courses.description: Equips learners with essential strategy and business skills to launch, manage, and grow successful ventures and prepare for disruption and change within the healthcare landscape. Students will learn to develop sustainable business models, create robust business plans, build and manage venture teams, explore financing options, and engage with investors in the healthcare ecosystem. Also explores the transformative ideas reshaping healthcare delivery and prepares students to evaluate those innovations to balance cost, quality, and access effectively. 4 graduate hours. No professional credit.
